# How exceptions accumulate · M06

Six-quarter accounting and capacity experiment. Move revealed requests between new, tailored, standard and retired lanes with pointer/touch or labelled selectors. Whole-quarter choices settle together; Undo includes settlement. Setup is paid once, upkeep and shared-surface friction recur, and expired benefit does not automatically remove upkeep.

New runs have a finite effort-day budget. Independent effort estimates cover setup, standardisation, maintenance, ageing, interactions and retirement; they are not converted from fictional value points. A plan exceeding its quarter’s budget cannot settle or earn outcomes. Remaining days serve named, divisible core work in arrival order, carrying unfinished work forward. The inspector traces effort and shows which items progress or wait. Its maintenance counterfactual holds the starting backlog and other changes fixed; it does not rewind history. Spare capacity can mean maintenance displaces no work.

Revealed effort estimates are editable until their first settlement. Shared effort rules and known core-work estimates are fixed after Q1; unsettled capacity budgets may change explicitly. Standard upkeep is 40% of base, pair effort falls to one third and related tailored setup can save up to 1.5 days. These are exposed modelling assumptions, not calibrated engineering estimates. Partial exception implementation, failure dynamics and a price for core work are outside this model.

Completed policy comparisons use identical effort estimates, budgets, value assumptions and progressively revealed requests. A rule that exceeds capacity is marked infeasible at that quarter, without claiming a completed-run value. Both automatic rules fail under the default budget; a selective manual run can complete. High capacity lets all core work fit, preserving a counterexample to inevitable displacement.

Earlier value-only saved runs retain their original accounting and remain playable. Capacity starts on an explicit replay; Undo restores the earlier run. Local persistence, recovery/cross-tab pause, decision notes and editable JSON/Markdown exports preserve assumptions and settlements. Import reconstructs outcomes from decisions and rejects inconsistent history before replacement. Tests cover legacy results, capacity conservation, queue carryover, retirement, reuse, effort edits, policy feasibility and portable work.
